subject: Re: GPU priming & activation — tactical onboarding plan
messages:
From: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@mediflow.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: onboarding@mediflow.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding kick — traffic profile + priming ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To get our Dedicated pool live on May 6 we need to lock the warm-pool priming schedule, autoscale thresholds, and a short runbook we can hand to our NetOps team. Attached is our 7‑day traffic profile (sampled by path) so you can recommend pool sizing and priming windows.

Key asks from our side:
- Recommended warm-pool size and priming timeline for initial cutover (US-east preferred).
- Autoscale thresholds (units and target latency) and expected cold-start behaviour during ramp.
- Clear netops playbook for VIP cutover and route changes (we need a short checklist we can give our infra team).

We also have a compliance gate: our security team will want to verify that KV cache handling and prefix caching policies won’t leak customer PII during priming. If you can call that out in the runbook, that would speed things up.

Attaching the traffic file and an internal calendar block for May 1–3 for any dry runs.

Thanks,
Sam Peterson
Head of Platform Engineering
MediFlow

Attachments: MediFlow_traffic_profile.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@mediflow.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding kick — traffic profile + priming ask

Sam — thanks for the clear asks and the traffic sample. High level plan below; I attached a concise activation checklist you can hand to NetOps.

Summary proposal (US-east primary):
- Warm-pool priming: provision 12 x A100-equivalent vGPUs (pool can be right-sized after first 72h). Run priming over two 3‑hour windows on May 2 (evening) and May 4 (morning) to exercise typical burst and batch flows.
- Autoscale policy: baseline min pool 4 GPUs, scale step +4, max 20 GPUs. Trigger on 95th percentile CPU+KV cache utilization or request queue > 120s; aim for token-level p99 latency < 350ms.
- Burst/backfill: allow cross-region fallback to US-west for bursts when us-east capacity > 80% and projected latency delta < 80ms. Fallback needs explicit netops approval at time of cutover.
- Data handling: priming will use synthetic prefixes only; we will not load customer KV items. We'll document prefix masking and a purge step in the runbook to satisfy your security team.

NetOps checklist (attached) includes: route shift steps, DNS TTL guidance, cutover rollback, and simple screens for validating KV purge. Connor will take ownership of the low-level runbook and can produce a NetOps-friendly doc.

Next steps:
1) Priyom to confirm resource availability for May 2/4 priming windows and sign off on autoscale knobs.
2) Connor to draft the netops_runbook_template with explicit purge commands and rollback commands.
3) Sam to confirm whether you want us to provision a warm pool in US-west as a warm standby (adds ~12–18 hours provisioning lead).

I attached: redwood_activation_checklist.pdf (short handover)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_activation_checklist.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@mediflow.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding kick — traffic profile + priming ask

Quick follow-up from engineering side:
- May 2 and May 4 windows work for compute — we can reserve the 12 A100-equivalent capacity in US-east for priming. We only need confirmation of the test payload (synthetic vs shadow) and the exact priming scripts.
- Autoscale knobs as Marissa suggested are fine, but we recommend the initial scaling trigger use queue depth + KV miss rate to avoid reactive overprovisioning. We'll ship a conservative config and monitor for 72h.
- For cross-region fallback: please confirm whether your infra team can accept session-affinity changes; otherwise we will use stateless fallbacks only.

Also adding a runbook draft to this thread — see attached netops_runbook_template.docx. It's intentionally short and prescriptive so your on-call can execute quickly.

Linking the HubSpot deal and SOW draft here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9342 — please sign the activation SOW by Apr 24 if the May 6 go‑live is needed.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: netops_runbook_template.docx
From: Kelsey Huang <kelsey@mediflow.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@mediflow.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding kick — traffic profile + priming ask

Thanks Priyom — the windows look good. A couple of clarifications from our NetOps lead: 
- We need the priming to avoid any production-state writes; synthetic payload only.
- For fallback, we can accept stateless route shifts but not session affinity changes during the first 7 days.
- Can you shorten the first priming window to 90 minutes and extend the second to 4 hours? Our busiest window is in the afternoon UTC.

If you can update the runbook with those two changes we can sign the SOW this week. We prefer DocuSign for the SOW link.

—Kelsey
Kelsey Huang
Infrastructure Lead, MediFlow

I'll also create the calendar invites for the May 2 and May 4 priming runs and include a 30m dry-run on Apr 30. Priyom — if you can grant me edit access to the reserved pool provisioning ticket (JIRA: INF-4127) I'll attach the exact GPU SKU and expected IP ranges.
